as_told.title: Menzel named in the MJ12 documents

plain: A scientist named Donald Menzel is named in the Majestic 12 papers, typed documents that describe a secret group of twelve said to have been set up under Truman to deal with UFOs. If the papers are genuine, a leading scientist sat on a hidden government UFO panel. The astronomer Beatriz Villarroel brings this up on the show without naming a source: look into Menzel, she says, and "suddenly you find that his name is famous" for these papers. Michels, in his own framing, says Menzel was named "as part of Truman's top secret UFO research panel in the late 1940s." The papers came to light on a roll of 35mm film that a man named Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and then studied with William Moore and Stanton Friedman. They were made public in 1987. The main paper presents itself as a briefing for Eisenhower dated 18 November 1952, with a 1947 Truman memo attached. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report finding no copy, the FBI's copies are marked "BOGUS" by hand, and an Air Force investigations office told the FBI it was "fabricated". The critic Philip Klass called the Truman memo a fraud, while Friedman judged both documents "almost certainly genuine". The briefing paper does list "Dr. Donald Menzel" among twelve members of a group it says Truman set up in September 1947, which fits Michels's late 1940s, and it says "some scientists, most notably Dr. Menzel, consider it more likely that we are dealing with beings from another solar system entirely." So both tellers report the naming as the paper makes it, and whether Menzel really served on such a panel depends on whether the paper is genuine.

discussion.text: A typed briefing paper dated 18 November 1952, with a Truman memorandum to Secretary Forrestal of 24 September 1947 as its Attachment A, that came to light on a roll of 35mm film Jaime Shandera received anonymously at his Burbank home in 1984 and that he, William Moore and Stanton Friedman then studied; it was made public in 1987. The National Archives and the Truman and Eisenhower Libraries report their searches for it negative. The FBI's Majestic 12 file holds copies sent to it in 1988 and 1991, each marked "BOGUS" by hand, and records that the Air Force Office of Special Investigations "advised on November 30, 1988, that the document was fabricated" and that "the document is completely bogus". Philip Klass called the Truman memo an obvious fraud; Friedman judged the briefing paper and the memo "almost certainly genuine". The briefing paper lists "Dr. Donald Menzel" among the twelve members of the group it says Truman established in September 1947, and its page 4 says "some scientists, most notably Dr. Menzel, consider it more likely that we are dealing with beings from another solar system entirely." The tellers report the naming as the paper makes it; that Menzel served on such a panel holds only as far as the paper is genuine.
